messages.content: does as small as mean the same as smaller than?
no. as small as can say two things have the same small size. smaller than says one is smaller.
give that explanation in fewer words.
as small as can say the two have the same small size. smaller than says one is smaller.
make it about two cups.
this cup is as small as that cup. this cup is smaller than that cup.
can both be true about the same two cups at the same moment?
not if you mean the same part of size at the same moment. one says the cups have the same size, and the other says they do not.
make that explanation shorter.
one says the cups have the same size. the other says they do not.
what if one cup can hold more water but both look the same from the front?
then you need to say which part of size you mean. looking the same from one side does not tell us how much each can hold.
only give a sentence about holding more water.
this cup can hold more water than that one.
does that mean it is full now?
no. how much it can hold is different from how much is inside now.
write a story about two people at a hotel both saying my room. show why the person at the desk needs more detail.

a woman came to the hotel desk and said she had left a book in her room. before she could say more, another person came down and said that his room needed a new towel. the worker asked each person which room they were using. both had said my room, but they were not talking about the same place. the woman gave the part of the building where her room was, and the worker checked her room before looking for the book. the other person gave his room detail too. later, both got the help they needed. the same small word had given a different place for each person.
why did my room not tell the worker enough?
my changes with the person saying it. the worker still needed to know which real room each person was using.
was one person wrong to call it my room?
no. each could use my for the room they were using. it did not mean the hotel was theirs.
make that explanation shorter.
my room can be the room someone is using, not a room they have as their own house.
write a useful question from the worker.
which room are you using?
why ask that instead of choosing one room?
because choosing without knowing could send help to the wrong place. the question gave the detail needed.
make that answer shorter.
the worker needed to know the room before choosing where to go.
finish with the book returned.
the worker brought the book to the woman, and she said thank you before going back to read.
we cooked together today. some parts were hard, but i liked having everyone in the kitchen.
you can like being together without saying every part was easy. what would you like to remember about it?
i want to remember my brother reading the page while my mother cooked and i put food on the table.
that gives you a clear picture of each person doing a different part of the meal.
write it in my voice, without saying the food was the best.
my brother read the page while my mother cooked, and i put food on the table. some parts were hard, but i liked being together in the kitchen.
can you make it one sentence?
i liked being in the kitchen with my family as my brother read, my mother cooked, and i put food on the table.
did that leave out the hard parts?
yes. it keeps the part you liked, but does not say that everything was easy. you can add that some things were hard if you want that detail too.
make that explanation shorter.
it leaves out the hard parts without saying they did not happen.
add them in a short way.
some parts were hard, but i liked being in the kitchen while my brother read, my mother cooked, and i put food on the table.
only give the first part about how i felt.
some parts were hard, but i liked being together.
five children are at a table with their mother and father. how many people are there?
seven people: five children and two parents.
if i also say the parents are there, does that add two more people?
not if the parents are the same mother and father you already gave. saying the parents does not add new people.
make that explanation shorter.
the parents are the same two people, so do not add them again.
now the grandmother comes too.
then there are eight people.
can you know all eight need their own chairs?
not from the number alone. you need to know whether each person needs their own chair and whether they can use another place such as a sofa.
make that answer shorter.
you need to know how they plan to sit.
all eight need their own chair, and there are six chairs. how many more do we need?
two more chairs.
what if two people choose to stand?
then six chairs could be enough if only six people sit. that is a change from having a chair for everyone.
only give the answer for six people sitting.
six chairs could be enough for six people sitting.
i am in the kitchen and my sister is in the garden. if i say come here, where do i want her to come?
to the kitchen, where you are.
if she says come here to me, is here still the kitchen?
no. here is about the place of the person talking. when she says it from the garden, here is the garden.
make that explanation shorter.
here can be a different place when a different person says it.
can we both say i am here and mean different places?
yes. you can say it in the kitchen, and she can say it in the garden. both sentences can be true.
what if i want a message that is clear without knowing where i am?
name the place. please come to the kitchen is more specific than come here.
now ask her if she wants me to go to the garden.
would you like me to come to the garden?
does that say she already asked?
no. you are asking now. you are not saying she already asked you to come.
only give the answer without an explanation.
no.
write a story about a child asking a question and then asking another before the first is answered. show a simple way to slow the conversation.

a child was looking at a map with his uncle. he asked where the school was, then asked how far it was from the park, then asked which road went home. his uncle began answering, but the child could not tell which answer went with which question. they stopped and chose one question to start with. his uncle showed the school, and the child showed him that place on the map himself. then they asked about the park. one question at a time helped them use the map, even though all the questions were useful.
what made the first answers hard to follow?
he asked more questions before getting the first answer. then he did not know which answer went with which question.
make that explanation shorter.
too many questions at once made the answers hard to follow.
what could he ask to start again?
could we do the school question first, then the rest?
make that question shorter.
could we do the school question first?
why was it useful to show where the school was?
it let him show that he understood that answer before moving to another question.
finish with the road home as the last question.
after they found the school and park, they looked for the road home. this time, he waited for that answer before asking more.
change we will read the book tomorrow to they, but keep the reading, book, and time.
they will read the book tomorrow.
explain what stayed the same.
the reading, the book, and tomorrow stayed the same. only we changed to they.
now make it about before now, using yesterday.
they read the book yesterday.
can you say who they are?
not from this sentence alone. they needs context to tell us which people you mean.
now i say they are my sister and brother.
your sister and brother read the book yesterday.
if i say my sister read and my brother listened, should the sentence stay the same?
no. that is a different detail about what each person did. say: my sister read the book yesterday, and my brother listened.
only give that sentence.
my sister read the book yesterday, and my brother listened.
why not say they both read?
you said one read and the other listened. changing both to reading would change the information you gave.
my friend is sitting alone. i want to ask if they want someone to sit with them, but do not say they must be lonely.
you could ask: would you like me to sit with you, or would you rather have some quiet time?
can i ask with fewer words?
would you like me to sit with you?
now give the choice to be alone too.
would you like me to sit with you, or would you rather be alone?
if they choose alone, should i say they do not like me?
no. the choice to be alone does not by itself say how they feel about you.
what can i say if they want to be alone?
okay. i will give you some time.
can that sound like i am waiting for them to finish being alone?
it could. you can keep the reply short without saying you are waiting: okay. take care.
only give the question again.
would you like me to sit with you, or would you rather be alone?
now just the short reply if they choose alone.
okay. take care.
